title: Residual Capacity: Structural Loss vs Functional Accessibility
caption: Figure 7. Residual capacity: structural loss versus functional accessibility. Two-column conceptual contrast separating documentable structural loss - tissue injury, synaptic loss, tauopathy, white matter damage, vascular injury, or neurodegenerative pathology - from functional accessibility, defined as whether surviving networks can coordinate, route, and express function under state-dependent conditions. Residual capacity is not a claim of tissue regeneration; it is a hypothesis about measurable network expression.
